transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

Um, I'm here because when I start eating, especially at night, I feel like I just can’t stop or control how much I’m eating anymore. It's like a switch flips and I can't control myself, and it's starting to really freak me out.

After these episodes where you feel you can't stop eating, do you ever do anything to try to prevent weight gain, such as making yourself throw up, using laxatives, fasting, or exercising excessively?

Yeah, I do, and I feel really ashamed about it. I'll go to the dorm bathroom and try to make myself throw up until my throat burns, or even take a bunch of laxatives because I'm terrified of seeing the weight on the scale the next morning. It's gotten to where I'm doing this at least a couple of times every week.
To help me understand your situation better, could you share your current height and weight, and whether you've recently lost a significant amount of weight?

I don't really know my exact height and weight off the top of my head. I don't think I've lost any weight, though—if anything, I feel like it's been creeping up on me, but I'm not sure of the actual numbers.
Has a doctor, family member, or friend ever expressed concern that you are too thin or underweight?

No, no one has ever said I'm too thin, and people usually tell me I look completely normal. But when I catch myself in the mirror, I still feel disgusted because all I can see is my stomach sticking out. It's like my whole worth is tied to whether I look lean enough that day.
How long have you been experiencing these weekly episodes of overeating followed by throwing up or using laxatives?

This whole cycle of losing control with food and then trying to undo it has been going on for about seven months, ever since I started community college. It really escalated to happening at least a couple of nights a week around midterms last fall.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient meets all diagnostic criteria for Bulimia Nervosa (F50.2). She reports recurrent episodes of binge eating characterized by a subjective loss of control, followed by inappropriate compensatory behaviors (self-induced vomiting and laxative abuse) to prevent weight gain. These episodes occur at least twice a week and have been ongoing for seven months. Furthermore, her self-evaluation is excessively influenced by her body shape and weight, and she does not meet the low weight criteria for Anorexia Nervosa.
